_evidence: Packet dispatcher 0x0054a3d3 (compose after ctr_0054a678, the 3-bit counter 0x7aafd0 every handler advances through 0x54ba6b; used WITHOUT fuzz, which randomised the handler table 0x833211 itself - the 'call cs:[ebx]' to 0x6548a9be/0x049942c2 faults). Length [0x7a97ac]: 'cmp ecx,1; jb' / 'cmp ecx,0x100; ja' reject 0 and > 0x100 (both drawn), in-range lengths are 9, 0x10, 0x2a, 0x100. Command byte [0x7a97b1]: any byte ('and al,0x80' sets 0x7aafd9; 'and eax,0x1f; cmp eax,0x1d; ja' rejects 0x1e/0x1f; 0x1a..0x1d share handler 0x1a with no length check). Commands below 0x1a must match the expected-length byte 0x83327d[cmd] ('cmp cl,[ebx]; jne'): those bytes are synthetic, 9 or 0x10 for the commands whose handlers run inside the emulator (0..4, 6, 0xa, 0xc..0x13, 0x15, 0x16, 0x18, 0x19: counter/flag stores, packet field copies, the 0x7c2a48 flag loop, the static 0x838c94 list walk of 0x54eb10), so the match falls through in about a quarter of those cases; the commands 5, 7, 8, 9, 0xb, 0x14, 0x17 get expected lengths 1..8, which the length domain never holds, because their handlers open message boxes (0x53c8c8 -> 0x536920 -> MessageBoxExA, unmodelled) or re-enter the packet pump 0x54a2c3: for them the dispatcher takes its reject path (the same 0x54a42b block as any length mismatch), and those handlers are left to the T2 in-game check. The 0x1a..0x1d handler 0x54a74c copies len-9 bytes from 0x7a97b6 ('rep movsb') to [0x824570 + 4*(cmd-0x1a)] + dword [0x7a97b2]: lengths 1..8 would make ecx wrap and fault the original (a block packet carries its 9-byte header), hence the length domain skips 1..8; the four destination pointers are 0x200-byte buffers and the offset dword is 0..0x108, so offset + 0xf7 stays inside; the copied bytes 0x7a97b6.. (0xf8) are random and the running total 0x828e7c ('add [esi],eax') is a random dword; 0x54fdde then sees [0x83e69e] = 0 (image) and returns. 0x7aafd9 starts at 0 or 0x12 so the 0xff store is visible.
